catalogue_metadata.scope_notes: Extracted from a Continuous Architecture Studio (CAS) system. The codebase demonstrates a hybrid approach where human-defined governance rules and agentic AI tools co-exist. Analysis limited to files listed in runtime context; several skills directories and subagent definitions were referenced but not fully inspected.
analysis_limits: Only code evidence from the provided file list was used; runtime traces and evaluations were not deeply analyzed.
Agent definitions in .agents/ and .claude/ directories were not fully explored; their SKILL.md and subagent markdown files were not inspected.
The cas-brain repository is referenced but not included in the analysis.

system_map.overview: The repository implements a Continuous Architecture Studio (CAS) platform that blends human-defined governance rules with agentic AI capabilities. It uses a centralised orchestrator (FlowRunner) to execute multi-step workflows, with an AgenticMerger to reconcile external agent contributions (e.g., Claude Code) into a consistent governance model. The system emphasises evidence-based knowledge management, compliance checking, and steering actions driven by predefined rules.

patterns.name: Governed Agentic Action

tool_protocols.notes: Relies on human-defined rules and LLM calls; no MCP or native tool calling.

optimisation_targets.notes: Governance rules ensure agent actions are controlled and aligned with enterprise standards.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Agents can act but within strict governance boundaries.

patterns.summary: Agentic actions are constrained by a governance layer that checks compliance and enforces rules before any AI-driven change is approved.
patterns.intent: Ensure that AI agents do not make uncontrolled changes to the architecture knowledge base or system configuration.
patterns.context: The CAS system integrates external agents (e.g., Claude Code) that propose modifications, but every change must pass through a compliance engine to verify it aligns with rules.
patterns.solution: A ComplianceEngine evaluates proposed changes against a set of rules defined in cas-knowledge/global/rules/. If violations are found, a GovernanceActionService generates a steering action, preventing the change from being applied.

evidence.note: Central point for checking agent actions against rules.

failure_modes: Overly restrictive if rules are not updated

patterns.reuse_notes: Adopt for any system where AI agents interact with business-critical resources and need to be constrained by enterprise policies.

patterns.name: Shared Context Pipeline

tool_protocols.notes: A single FlowRunner executes a sequence of steps, passing a shared context object.

optimisation_targets.notes: Ensures consistent data handoff between steps.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Centralised pipeline reduces complexity and makes execution deterministic.

patterns.summary: A central flow runner executes a sequence of steps, passing a shared context object that is mutated by each step, ensuring consistent state propagation.
patterns.intent: Execute multi-step agentic workflows in a linear fashion while maintaining a single execution context.
patterns.context: The CAS runner orchestrates steps like rule evaluation, LLM calls, and knowledge updates. Each step reads and writes to a Context object.
patterns.solution: FlowRunner maintains a context that is passed to each step. Steps can modify it, and the next step receives the updated context. This is a common pattern in pipeline-based agentic systems.

evidence.note: Implements the pipeline loop and context passing.

failure_modes: Context mutation bugs if steps not careful

patterns.reuse_notes: Applicable to any workflow engine where steps need to share state.

patterns.name: LLM Provider Abstraction

tool_protocols.notes: Uses a client class to abstract LLM interactions, allowing swapping providers.

optimisation_targets.notes: Allows cost optimization by choosing different providers (e.g., mock vs real).

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Abstraction enables switching between autonomous LLM and deterministic mock.

patterns.summary: LLM interactions are abstracted behind a client interface, allowing the system to use different providers (real or mock) without changing the orchestration logic.
patterns.intent: Decouple agentic workflows from specific LLM providers to improve flexibility and testability.
patterns.context: The system defines a common interface (LiteLLMClient and MockLLMClient) that returns LLM responses for prompts. The runner depends on this interface, not a concrete provider.
patterns.solution: Define a client protocol using Pydantic or ABC, with concrete implementations for LiteLLM and mock responses. The orchestrator uses this interface.
patterns.reuse_notes: Apply to any agentic system that interacts with LLMs to enable testing and cost control.

patterns.name: Governance as Code

tool_protocols.notes: Rules are codified in YAML files and enforced programmatically.

optimisation_targets.notes: Ensures consistent enforcement of rules across environments.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Rules are explicit and deterministic, reducing ambiguity.

patterns.summary: Governance rules and architecture constraints are defined as machine-readable YAML files that are parsed and enforced by a compliance engine.
patterns.intent: Make governance rules explicit, versioned, and automatically enforceable against agent actions.
patterns.context: The CAS system stores rules in cas-knowledge/global/rules/ and uses ComplianceEngine to check for violations.
patterns.solution: Rules are written in YAML with a schema (JSON Schema validation). The compliance engine loads these rules and evaluates repository state against them.

failure_modes: Rules may become stale relative to system evolution

patterns.reuse_notes: Adopt for any system where policies need to be machine-checkable and versioned.

patterns.name: Agent Contract Schema Validation

tool_protocols.notes: Uses Pydantic models and JSON schemas to validate data exchanged between agents.

optimisation_targets.notes: Ensures agent outputs conform to expected structure, reducing errors.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Agents are free to produce outputs but must conform to defined schemas.

patterns.summary: Inter-agent communications are validated against Pydantic models and JSON schemas, ensuring that agent outputs meet expected contracts before being merged into the system.
patterns.intent: Prevent malformed data from entering the governance system and ensure type safety across agent boundaries.
patterns.context: When an external agent (e.g., Claude) generates a proposal for architecture changes, the AgenticMerger validates it against expected Pydantic models; if validation fails, the change is rejected.
patterns.solution: Define all inter-agent data structures as Pydantic models. Use Pydantic's validation to parse and validate incoming agent outputs.

evidence.note: Uses schemas to validate and merge.

failure_modes: Over-strict schemas might reject legitimate agent outputs

patterns.reuse_notes: Use Pydantic/JSON Schema validation for all agent communication to ensure data integrity.

patterns.name: Orchestration via CLI and CI

tool_protocols.notes: Agent workflows are triggered via CLI commands or CI workflows.

optimisation_targets.notes: Automation of agentic processes via CI ensures consistent execution.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Centralised orchestration via CLI/CI makes the system predictable and easy to manage.

patterns.summary: Agentic workflows are invoked through a CLI or CI/CD pipelines, providing a deterministic entry point for automation.
patterns.intent: Expose agentic capabilities as command-line tools and CI jobs so they can be automated and versioned.
patterns.context: The CAS runner has a CLI (main function) and GitHub Actions workflows that invoke the runner for tasks like building steering projections or validating changes.
patterns.solution: Implement a CLI that parses commands and calls the FlowRunner. Define CI workflows that run these CLI commands on events.
patterns.reuse_notes: Expose agentic systems via CLI and CI for easy integration into developer workflows.

patterns.name: Health and Risk Monitoring

tool_protocols.notes: Uses metrics and health models to evaluate system state.

optimisation_targets.notes: Continuous monitoring helps detect problems early.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Explicit metrics and health checks provide transparency.

patterns.summary: The system computes health scores and governance risks to evaluate the state of the architecture and guide agent decisions.
patterns.intent: Provide quantitative measures of system health and governance compliance to inform agentic actions.
patterns.context: HealthStatus and get_health_reasons functions calculate a health score based on compliance findings; GovernanceHealth in models.py aggregates governance metrics.
patterns.solution: Implement functions that compute health metrics from data (e.g., compliance findings). Expose these via dashboard or APIs.

failure_modes: Metrics may be misleading if thresholds are wrong

patterns.reuse_notes: Use health metrics to drive agentic decisions and trigger remediation actions.

patterns.name: Evidence-First Knowledge Management

tool_protocols.notes: Knowledge is structured with evidence files and templates, emphasizing decorrelation.

optimisation_targets.notes: Ensures claims are grounded in evidence.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Using templates and evidence requirements reduces ambiguity.

patterns.summary: Architecture knowledge is stored with mandatory evidence references, ensuring that agent-generated claims are traceable to actual code or decisions.
patterns.intent: Prevent hallucination and unverified claims in architecture documentation by requiring evidence.
patterns.context: All rules, patterns, and signals in cas-knowledge have templates that include evidence fields. Agents are expected to fill these out with concrete references.
patterns.solution: Knowledge templates enforce that every entry includes an evidence section, typically linking to files or commits. The compliance engine can verify that evidence is present.

evidence.note: Template for rules with evidence requirements.

failure_modes: Agents may provide fake or irrelevant evidence

patterns.reuse_notes: Implement evidence checks in any agentic system that generates documentation to ensure accuracy.

patterns.name: Capability-Based State Model

tool_protocols.notes: Tracks capabilities and their lineage to understand system evolution.

optimisation_targets.notes: Deep understanding of system capabilities enables better governance.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Modeling capabilities provides structure but allows flexibility.

patterns.summary: The system models architecture state as a set of capabilities, each with lineage information, enabling traceability and impact analysis.
patterns.intent: Represent the architecture in terms of capabilities to enable more profound analysis and agentic reasoning.
patterns.context: SteeringRuntimeIndex comprises CapabilityRecord objects, each with CapabilityLineage, allowing the system to trace how capabilities evolved.
patterns.solution: Define a data model with capability categories, records, and lineage. Propel the runtime index with this data.
patterns.reuse_notes: Use capability models for any system that needs to track architecture evolution.

patterns.name: Human-in-the-Loop Approval

tool_protocols.notes: Some actions require manual approval before execution.

optimisation_targets.notes: Ensures sensitive changes are reviewed by humans.

patterns.summary: Certain governance actions require human approval before they are executed, preventing automatic modification of critical resources.
patterns.intent: Maintain human oversight over high-risk agentic actions.
patterns.context: GovernanceActionEngine has a TransitionRegistry that defines allowed transitions; likely some transitions require manual approval.
patterns.solution: Implement a registry of actions that are tagged as 'requires_approval'. If such an action is proposed, the system holds it until a human approves.

evidence.note: Registry of state transitions, possibly with approval requirements.

failure_modes: Bottleneck if too many approvals required

patterns.reuse_notes: Identify high-risk actions and route them through a human approval step.

patterns.name: Agentic Validation Workflows

tool_protocols.notes: Automated scripts check for compliance and correctness as part of CI.

patterns.summary: Automated scripts and CI workflows validate agentic outputs, enforcing conformity to coding standards and governance rules.
patterns.intent: Ensure that changes (including agent-generated ones) meet predefined quality and governance thresholds before integration.
patterns.context: The repository includes validation scripts that check YAML syntax, hardcoding, unpinned installers, etc., and CI workflows run them on every change.
patterns.solution: Implement validation scripts as part of the CI pipeline. These scripts run automated checks and fail the build if issues are detected.
patterns.reuse_notes: Embed automated validation in CI to enforce contracts and governance.

patterns.name: Centralised Governance Engine

tool_protocols.notes: A dedicated engine encapsulates all governance logic.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Centralised logic is easier to maintain.

patterns.summary: All governance decisions are processed through a single engine, ensuring consistent application of rules and actions.
patterns.intent: Provide a single source of truth for governance checks and actions, avoiding scattered logic.
patterns.context: ComplianceEngine and GovernanceActionEngine are the only components that interact with governance rules.
patterns.solution: Route all compliance checks and action generation through dedicated engine classes.

failure_modes: Single point of failure if engine fails

patterns.reuse_notes: Centralise governance logic to ensure consistent enforcement.
